sections.h2: Edmonton offices that run Metcalfe County tax
sections.html:
In Metcalfe County the PVA appraises, the sheriff mails the bill and takes the payment, and the county clerk inherits any bill left open in the spring. The PVA's website, hosted on qpublic.net, publishes the roll and a tax calendar.

Edmonton is the county seat and the only incorporated city.

• Sheriff: bills and collections. P.O. Box 371, Edmonton, KY 42129, phone (270) 432-3041.
  • PVA: values, exemption forms, mailing address changes. P.O. Box 939, phone (270) 432-3162, website www.qpublic.net/ky/metcalfe.
  • Fiscal Court: county government, at 201 North Main, with a mailing box at P.O. Box 149, phone (270) 432-3181.
  • County Attorney: P.O. Box 999, phone (270) 432-0777.

Lien and delinquent bill details come from the county clerk's office. A new owner who never receives a bill should contact the sheriff.

State law (KRS 134.015) sets November 1 as the end of the 2 percent discount. Metcalfe County's tax calendar runs a little differently in places, so read the dates printed on your own bill and confirm with the sheriff before relying on a later one.

Metcalfe County tax calendar
Date or periodWhat happens
September 15Sheriff has the bills in hand
January5 percent added
February onward10 percent added, plus a 10 percent sheriff fee
April 15, close of businessBills pass from sheriff to clerk
July 14 to August 28Window for the clerk's certificate sale
September 1Sheriff's settlement due

sections.h2: Who buys homes in Metcalfe County
sections.html:
Metcalfe covers about 290 square miles of south central Kentucky. It was organized in May 1860 as the 106th Kentucky county. It sits in the Glasgow micropolitan area, so a seller may meet buyers who work toward Glasgow or Bowling Green. Edmonton lies on the Louis B. Nunn Cumberland Parkway, about 29 miles from Interstate 65, with Glasgow 16 miles west and Louisville 113 miles away.

The county had 10,286 residents in 2020 and an estimate of 10,583 for mid-2025. Edmonton had about 1,586 residents in 2010 against 10,099 for the whole county, so most owners live outside the city. The 2020 count showed 4,691 housing units, 11.6 percent of them empty. A typical owner-occupied home is worth $110,200 and typical rent is $582. Homeowners live in 77.7 percent of homes, and owner costs run $1,066 a month with a mortgage and $368 with none. About 19.0 percent of residents are 65 or older, which is the group that can claim the homestead exemption.

Start with the PVA while the roll is on public view, which runs 13 days from the first Monday of May and includes Saturdays. If the conference fails, go to the county clerk, and do it by the next workday after the viewing period closes.

The appeals board has three local members, named by the mayor of the county's largest city, the fiscal court and the judge executive. Since Edmonton is the only city, its mayor makes one of those picks. A change by the board must come with a written explanation, and you may record the hearing. Bring:

  • Sale prices and dates of similar homes near yours.
  • A contractor quote for repairs that the PVA record omits.
  • The dollar value you claim, written on the form.

If you file and then skip the hearing, you can't take the appeal further.

State rules send PVAs to every parcel at least every four years and put new buildings on the roll each year. Farm land can be assessed at what it is worth as agriculture instead of its fair cash value.

On nearly 290 square miles with about 10,500 residents, many Metcalfe County sales include acreage. If any part of a parcel is farmed, ask the PVA about its classification before you list.

An owner who turns 65 during the year, or is classified as totally disabled on January 1, applies at the PVA for the home they own and live in. KRS 132.810 allows a single exemption for each residential unit and includes mobile homes and manufactured houses.

A disabled owner under 65 reapplies yearly, except someone with a service-connected total disability or a permanent disability finding. Applying before payment reduces the bill, and applying afterward earns a refund.

Unpaid bills reach the clerk's office at the end of April 15 as certificates of delinquency, each with a lien on record. Interest of 1 percent a month builds up, and clerk and county attorney fees of 10 and 20 percent follow. A public listing is required at least 30 days before the sale.

The January 1 owner is personally liable, and the lien can trail the property for 11 years. A private buyer who gets the certificate collects from the owner and may add fees.

It doesn't have to stop a sale. The sheriff quotes the payoff before April 15 and the clerk afterward, and the amount grows monthly once the clerk has it. Request a written figure dated close to closing.

January 1 settles tax ownership, so a late-year sale leaves the bill with the previous owner until next year. Many Metcalfe County sellers hold older houses with repairs put off. To weigh a cash offer against a listing, work out each net after repairs, tax and months of carrying cost.

Before you list, gather your deed, latest bill and any exemption approval. Call the PVA to check the acreage and building description, and ask the sheriff for the current balance. If the house is inherited, bring the papers showing who may sign. After closing, tell the PVA the new owner's name so the bill is mailed to the right place.

A typical Metcalfe County sale runs in a clear order. First, confirm with the PVA what is on record for the parcel, including any homestead claim and the farm classification if there is acreage. Second, ask the sheriff for the bill and the balance. If April 15 has passed, ask the clerk instead, because the bill has moved there. Third, decide in the contract who pays the year's tax, since the January 1 owner is the one on the bill. Fourth, give the closing agent a written payoff dated close to the closing day so the tax is settled out of the sale money.

Roads matter in this county. Edmonton is on the parkway and U.S. 68, with Kentucky routes 80 and 163 also serving the town, so buyers commuting to Glasgow or Bowling Green often judge a house by drive time. Mention the route and distance in your listing. A cash buyer can skip the repair list that a lender might require, which helps with older houses where work was put off, but expect a lower price in exchange for that speed.

faqs.q: Who takes payment of Metcalfe County property tax?
faqs.a: The county sheriff, whose mailing box is P.O. Box 371 in Edmonton. The phone is (270) 432-3041.

faqs.q: Is there a city property tax in Edmonton?
faqs.a: Edmonton is the county's only incorporated city. Call the Fiscal Court at (270) 432-3181 to ask whether a city bill applies to your parcel.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Metcalfe County PVA?
faqs.a: Call (270) 432-3162 or write to P.O. Box 939, Edmonton, KY 42129. The office site is www.qpublic.net/ky/metcalfe.

faqs.q: When can a Metcalfe County owner contest a value?
faqs.a: During the 13 days that begin on the first Monday of May. A PVA conference has to come before any filing.

faqs.q: How long does a delinquent tax lien last?
faqs.a: Up to 11 years under KRS 134.015, through any change of owner.
